content: 1. Both in and vorinostat are known to increase the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid their concurrent use or consider alternative medications. 2. Clarithromycin can elevate the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by interfering with hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 3. Omeprazole can increase the levels or effects of warfarin through mechanisms other than CYP enzymes. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Warfarin’s less potent R-enantiomer is partially metabolized by CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19. 4. Clarithromycin can also increase the levels or effects of warfarin through mechanisms other than CYP enzymes. Use caution and monitor closely. If co-administered with inhibitors of these isoenzymes, monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 5. Zafirlukast can increase the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of zaleplon by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Reduce zanubrutinib to 80 mg twice daily when co-administered with clarithromycin 250 mg twice daily, or to 80 mg once daily with clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily. Resume the previous zanubrutinib dose after discontinuing clarithromycin. 8. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of intranasal zavegepant through mechanisms involving OATP1B3 inhibition, leading to significant systemic exposure. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of zidovudine through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Clarithromycin may either increase or decrease zidovudine levels, as conflicting reports exist in the literature. Separate administration by at least 2 to 4 hours. 10. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of ziprasidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both clarithromycin and ziprasidone increase the QTc interval, so avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of zolpidem by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of zonisamide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of zuranolone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Reduce the zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis and other urogenital effects, such as hematuria, proteinuria, elevated serum creatinine, microscopic pyuria, urinary tract infection, glycosuria, urinary frequency, testicular pain, and erectile dysfunction, may occur. Refer to individual drug monographs for more information. 15. Co-administration of clarithromycin with pimozide, ergotamine, or dihydroergotamine is contraindicated. 16. Based on animal studies, omeprazole and clarithromycin during pregnancy may cause fetal harm. Therapy is not recommended for pregnant women unless no alternative therapy is appropriate. If administered during pregnancy or if pregnancy occurs during therapy, the patient should be informed of the potential hazard to the fetus. 17. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies of omeprazole, clarithromycin, or amoxicillin (used separately or together) in pregnant women. 18. Limited human data indicate that clarithromycin and its active metabolite, 14-OH clarithromycin, are present in human milk at less than 2% of the maternal weight-adjusted dose. Observational studies report adverse effects on breastfed children (rash, diarrhea, loss of appetite, somnolence) comparable to amoxicillin. 19. No data are available to assess the effects of clarithromycin or 14-OH clarithromycin on milk production. 20. Limited data from a single case report suggest that omeprazole may be present in human milk. There are no clinical data on the effects of omeprazole on breastfed infants or milk production. 21. Published clinical lactation studies indicate that amoxicillin is present in human milk. Reported adverse effects in breastfed infants include diarrhea. There are no data on the effects of amoxicillin on milk production. 22. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered alongside the mother’s clinical need for omeprazole, clarithromycin, or amoxicillin, and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child from these drugs or the underlying maternal condition. 23. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk, making the therapy generally acceptable. 24.
